title: How to create forms with Server Actions

description: Learn how to create forms in Next.js with React Server Actions.

React Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.

> [!WARNING]
> Always verify [authentication and authorization](/docs/app/guides/authentication) inside each Server Action, even if the form is only rendered on an authenticated page. See the [Data Security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security) for more details.

## How it works

React extends the HTML [`<form>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [`action`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.

When used in a form, the function automatically receives the [`FormData`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [`FormData` methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):

title: refresh

`refresh` allows you to refresh the client router from within a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).

## Usage

`refresh` can **only** be called from within Server Actions. It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.

## Parameters

```tsx
refresh(): void;
```

## Returns

`refresh` does not return a value.

00004| ---
00005| 
00006| `revalidatePath` allows you to invalidate [cached data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) on-demand for a specific path.
00007| 
00008| ## Usage
00009| 
00010| `revalidatePath` can be called in Server Functions and Route Handlers.
00011| 
00012| `revalidatePath` cannot be called in Client Components or Proxy, as it only works in server environments.
00013| 
00014| > **Good to know**:
00015| >
00016| > - **Server Functions**: Updates the UI immediately (if viewing the affected path). Currently, it also causes all previously visited pages to refresh when navigated to again. This behavior is temporary and will be updated in the future to apply only to the specific path.
00017| > - **Route Handlers**: Marks the path for revalidation. The revalidation is done on the next visit to the specified path. This means calling `revalidatePath` with a dynamic route segment will not immediately trigger many revalidations at once. The invalidation only happens when the path is next visited.
00018| 
00019| ## Parameters
00020| 
00021| ```tsx
00022| revalidatePath(path: string, type?: 'page' | 'layout'): void;
00023| ```
00024| 
00025| - `path`: Either a string that represents your route file structure. This can be a literal path like `/product/123`, or a route pattern with dynamic segments like `/product/[slug]`. Do not append `/page` or `/layout`, use the `type` parameter instead. Must not exceed 1024 characters. This value is case-sensitive. You do not need to include a trailing slash, regardless of your [`trailingSlash`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/trailingSlash) config.
00026| - `type`: (optional) `'page'` or `'layout'` string to change the type of path to revalidate. If `path` contains a dynamic segment, for example `/product/[slug]`, this parameter is required. If `path` is a literal path like `/product/1`, omit `type`.
00027| 
00028| Use a literal path when you want to refresh a [single page](#revalidating-a-specific-path). Use a route pattern plus `type` to refresh [all matching pages](#revalidating-a-page-path).
00029| 
00030| ## Returns
00031| 
00032| `revalidatePath` does not return a value.
00033| 
00034| ## What can be invalidated
00035| 
00036| The path parameter can point to pages, layouts, or route handlers:
00037| 
00038| - **Pages**: Invalidates the specific page
00039| - **Layouts**: Invalidates the layout (the `layout.tsx` at that segment), all nested layouts beneath it, and all pages beneath them
00040| - **Route Handlers**: Invalidates cached data accessed within route handlers. For example `revalidatePath("/api/data")` invalidates this GET handler:
00041| 
00042| ```ts filename="app/api/data/route.ts"
00043| export async function GET() {
00044|   const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog', {
00045|     cache: 'force-cache',
00046|   })
00047| 
00048|   return Response.json(await data.json())
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ## Using `revalidatePath` with rewrites
00053| 
00054| When using [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites), you must pass the **destination** path (the actual route file location), not the source path that appears in the browser's address bar.
00055| 
00056| For example, if you have a rewrite from `/blog` to `/news`:
00057| 
00058| ```js filename="next.config.js"
00059| module.exports = {
00060|   async rewrites() {
00061|     return [
00062|       {
00063|         source: '/blog',
00064|         destination: '/news',
00065|       },
00066|     ]
00067|   },
00068| }
00069| ```
00070| 
00071| To revalidate this page, use the destination path:
00072| 
00073| ```ts
00074| // Correct: use the destination path
00075| revalidatePath('/news')
00076| 
00077| // Incorrect: the source path won't match the cache entry
00078| revalidatePath('/blog')
00079| ```
00080| 
00081| This is because `revalidatePath` operates on the route file structure, not the URL visible to users. Cache entries are tagged based on which route file renders them.
00082| 
00083| ## Relationship with `revalidateTag` and `updateTag`
00084| 
00085| `revalidatePath`, [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) and [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) serve different purposes:
00086| 
00087| - **`revalidatePath`**: Invalidates a specific page or layout path
00088| - **`revalidateTag`**: Marks data with specific tags as **stale**. Applies across all pages that use those tags
00089| - **`updateTag`**: Expires data with specific tags. Applies across all pages that use those tags
00090| 
00091| When you call `revalidatePath`, only the specified path gets fresh data on the next visit. Other pages that use the same data tags will continue to serve cached data until those specific tags are also revalidated:
00092| 
00093| ```tsx
00094| // Page A: /blog
00095| const posts = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog', {
00096|   next: { tags: ['posts'] },
00097| })
00098| 
00099| // Page B: /dashboard
00100| const recentPosts = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog?limit=5', {
00101|   next: { tags: ['posts'] },
00102| })
00103| ```
00104| 
00105| After calling `revalidatePath('/blog')`:
00106| 
00107| - **Page A (/blog)**: Shows fresh data (page re-rendered)
00108| - **Page B (/dashboard)**: Still shows stale data (cache tag 'posts' not invalidated)
00109| 
00110| Learn about the difference between [`revalidateTag` and `updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#differences-from-revalidatetag).
00111| 
00112| ### Building revalidation utilities
00113| 
00114| `revalidatePath` and `updateTag` are complementary primitives that are often used together in utility functions to ensure comprehensive data consistency across your application:
00115| 
00116| ```ts
00117| 'use server'
00118| 
00119| import { revalidatePath, updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00120| 
00121| export async function updatePost() {
00122|   await updatePostInDatabase()
00123| 
00124|   revalidatePath('/blog') // Refresh the blog page
00125|   updateTag('posts') // Refresh all pages using 'posts' tag
00126| }
00127| ```
00128| 
00129| This pattern ensures that both the specific page and any other pages using the same data remain consistent.
00130| 
00131| ## Examples
00132| 
00133| ### Revalidating a specific path
00134| 
00135| ```ts
00136| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00137| revalidatePath('/blog/post-1')
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| This will invalidate one specific path for revalidation on the next page visit.
00141| 
00142| ### Revalidating a Page path
00143| 
00144| ```ts
00145| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00146| revalidatePath('/blog/[slug]', 'page')
00147| // or with route groups
00148| revalidatePath('/(main)/blog/[slug]', 'page')
00149| ```
00150| 
00151| This will invalidate any path that matches the provided `page` file for revalidation on the next page visit. This will _not_ invalidate pages beneath the specific page. For example, `/blog/[slug]` won't invalidate `/blog/[slug]/[author]`.
00152| 
00153| ### Revalidating a Layout path
00154| 
00155| ```ts
00156| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00157| revalidatePath('/blog/[slug]', 'layout')
00158| // or with route groups
00159| revalidatePath('/(main)/post/[slug]', 'layout')
00160| ```
00161| 
00162| This will invalidate any path that matches the provided `layout` file for revalidation on the next page visit. This will cause pages beneath with the same layout to be invalidated and revalidated on the next visit. For example, in the above case, `/blog/[slug]/[another]` would also be invalidated and revalidated on the next visit.
00163| 
00164| ### Revalidating all data
00165| 
00166| ```ts
00167| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00168| 
00169| revalidatePath('/', 'layout')
00170| ```
00171| 
00172| This will purge the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache), and invalidate all cached data for revalidation on the next page visit.
00173| 
00174| ### Server Function
00175| 
00176| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
00177| 'use server'
00178| 
00179| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00180| 
00181| export default async function submit() {
00182|   await submitForm()
00183|   revalidatePath('/')
00184| }
00185| ```
00186| 
00187| ### Route Handler
00188| 
00189| ```ts filename="app/api/revalidate/route.ts" switcher
00190| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00191| import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
00192| 
00193| export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
00194|   const path = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('path')
00195| 
00196|   if (path) {
00197|     revalidatePath(path)
00198|     return Response.json({ revalidated: true, now: Date.now() })
00199|   }
00200| 
00201|   return Response.json({
00202|     revalidated: false,
00203|     now: Date.now(),
00204|     message: 'Missing path to revalidate',
00205|   })
00206| }
00207| ```
00208| 
00209| ```js filename="app/api/revalidate/route.js" switcher

title: revalidatePath
description: API Reference for the revalidatePath function.
---

`revalidatePath` allows you to invalidate [cached data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) on-demand for a specific path.

## Usage

`revalidatePath` can be called in Server Functions and Route Handlers.

`revalidatePath` cannot be called in Client Components or Proxy, as it only works in server environments.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - **Server Functions**: Updates the UI immediately (if viewing the affected path). Currently, it also causes all previously visited pages to refresh when navigated to again. This behavior is temporary and will be updated in the future to apply only to the specific path.
> - **Route Handlers**: Marks the path for revalidation. The revalidation is done on the next visit to the specified path. This means calling `revalidatePath` with a dynamic route segment will not immediately trigger many revalidations at once. The invalidation only happens when the path is next visited.

In an `action` or mutation context, they are also called **Server Actions**.

Created `app/actions.ts` with `toggleNotificationPreference` (a Server Action that flips the preference and calls `refresh` from `next/cache`), and updated `app/page.tsx` to read the current state and submit the form. Type check passes.

Key points per the docs (`next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/07-mutating-data.md:378`):
- `refresh` is imported from `next/cache` (not `next/navigation`).
- It can only be called from a Server Action.
- It refreshes the client router on the current page — no redirect, no path argument needed.
